source:
This is a major update to Soundscape.

Travel mode is much improved. When you travel by car or bus, Soundscape now calls out road numbers, your direction of travel, and nearby settlements. It also calls out when you cross rivers, canals, firths, and bays. Please update your offline maps to get these new features. Bus stop descriptions are now much better for users in the UK.

Sleep mode can now wake automatically when it detects that you are moving again. You no longer need to remember to wake it yourself.

We reorganized the underlying code so that we can build an iOS app from the same code. This means that in the future, we can release an iOS app with all of the features we have built for Android.

Please continue to report any problems, however small, through Contact Support in the main menu.
current: Questo è un importante aggiornamento di Soundscape. La modalità Viaggio è molto migliorata. Quando viaggi in auto o in autobus, Soundscape ora annuncia i numeri delle strade, la tua direzione di marcia e i centri abitati vicini. Annuncia anche quando attraversi fiumi, canali, estuari e baie. Aggiorna le tue mappe offline per ottenere queste nuove funzionalità. Le descrizioni delle fermate degli autobus sono ora molto migliori per gli utenti nel Regno Unito. La modalità Sospendi ora può riattivarsi automaticamente quando rileva che ti stai muovendo di nuovo. Non devi più ricordarti di riattivarla manualmente. Abbiamo riorganizzato il codice sottostante in modo da poter creare un'app iOS a partire dallo stesso codice. Questo significa che in futuro potremo rilasciare un'app iOS con tutte le funzionalità che abbiamo creato per Android. Continua a segnalarci eventuali problemi, per quanto piccoli, tramite l'opzione Contatta l'assistenza nel menu principale.

source: Welcome to the guided tutorial. This tutorial will guide you through the main features of the app. You can stop the tutorial at any time by tapping Cancel Guided Tutorial in the Main Menu. Let's start with Places Nearby. It lets you find points of interest. The Places Nearby button is on the Home screen, just below the Search bar. Tap it now to try it.

source: Callout detail controls how much Soundscape tells you about as you walk. Detailed mode calls out everything nearby. Simplified mode leaves out minor paths and service roads, and repeats itself less often. Essential mode calls out streets, junctions and landmarks only. Silent mode makes no automatic callouts at all, leaving beacons, routes and the buttons on the home screen.

source: If you take a bus route regularly, save your pickup and exit stops as Markers. This saves them so you can find them again easily. Go to *Markers and Routes* from the home screen, then find them on the *Markers* page. You can set a beacon on them to get periodic updates on how close you are to your exit stop. Note: you can turn off the rhythmic sound and still get distance updates along the way.

«Orientamento» is the general word (orientation, guidance). As a POI it's ambiguous, especially in an orientation app. The sport is called «orienteering» in Italian (FISO).

«Drogheria» in current Italian means a grocer/spice shop. The comment describes a store selling medicines, toiletries and convenience items, which Italians call a «parafarmacia». Needs a native check.
«Paese» is the usual word for a village, and «Villaggio» (osm_village) sounds like a holiday village. Suggest town «Cittadina», village «Paese», keeping hamlet «Frazione». Needs a native check.

source: Why does the audible beacon disappear sometimes?
current: Perché a volte l'audiofaro acustico scompare?
suggested: Perché a volte l'audiofaro acustico scompare?
reason: «audiofaro acustico» is a tautology (C2): «audio-» already makes it acoustic. Same in faq_why_does_beacon_disappear_answer. It's Microsoft's baseline wording (C14), so it's flagged for the reviewer rather than changed. The fix would be to drop «acustico».

«Passaggio sopra %1$s» puts a bare name after «sopra», so a river name comes out without its article («sopra Tevere»). The marker system only covers a/di/da/in/su. Flagged for the reviewer, together with directions_going_under_railway (the same «sotto %1$s»).
